- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates downside; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for early correction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 79.0), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to ≤10% of spike magnitude.  
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 5% below recent 10-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment to final 5–7 forecast points.  
- If sentiment history includes alternating bullish/bearish signals, model often misreads momentum; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
